prs.title: test(bindings): build the burst before the first send
prs.body:
## What

One flaky Android test, on main since #465: `PeerStreamSocketsTest > a burst to a reading peer is not dropped`. It failed on #466's first CI run (a PR that touches no Android code), passed on re-run, and passed on main's own run and both #465 runs.

## Why it flakes

The test sends eight 1 MiB frames and asserts all eight are `QUEUED`. It built each frame between sends:

```kotlin
val results = (0 until 8).map { a.send("peer-b", ByteArray(1_048_576) { it.toByte() }) }
```

`enqueue` refuses a frame only when the queue is over its 4 MiB budget (from the fifth send) **and** the writer has been blocked on one 64 KiB piece longer than `writeStallMs`, which the test's fast limits set to 100 ms. The peer does not read until the sends are done, so the writer fills both loopback buffers and blocks during the first frame. From then on, anything slow on the test thread between two sends counts toward the stall threshold. Four arrays of a million elements built by a cold JIT on a shared runner is enough.

Reproduced locally on the CI harness by adding a 150 ms pause between the fourth and fifth send, which yields the CI failure verbatim:

```
expected:<[QUEUED x8]> but was:<[QUEUED, QUEUED, QUEUED, QUEUED, QUEUE_FULL, QUEUE_FULL, QUEUE_FULL, QUEUE_FULL]>
```

## The fix

Build the eight frames first, then send them back to back, which is what the test's own comment ("eight ceiling frames in one tick") describes. Eight enqueues take microseconds, so the writer cannot pass a 100 ms stall threshold between them. The comment now says why.

No production code changes. The bound's behaviour under a real stall is covered by the neighbouring test and is unchanged.

## Verification

Full Android suite on the CI harness from this branch: 552 tests, 0 failures. The pause-between-sends variant fails on main's test and cannot be applied to this one, since there is no longer anything between sends.

prs.title: test(mls): a conformance suite for MlsStorage
prs.body:
## What

A conformance suite for `MlsStorage`, the trait every binding implements for key material, at `offline_protocol_mls::storage_conformance::run` and re-exported as `offline_protocol::mls_storage_conformance` beside the protocol-state suite. Same report shape, same rule: green is the definition of supported.

Nothing has ever held an `MlsStorage` to the contract the engine relies on. The protocol-state suite exercises the in-memory store only through a test adapter, and the trait's two defaulted methods, its colon-bearing session ids and its concurrency clause were never probed at all.

## The checks

Seventeen, each with a negative control in the suite's own tests (one injected defect per check, `Faulty` in `storage_conformance.rs`), so a check that stops catching its defect fails CI, and so does a check added without a control. Forcing each check to pass in turn fails the tests for all seventeen.

Key-type isolation runs first, with point writes and deletes of ids nothing else uses, and a failure ends the run before any listed delete. Without that, a backend that merges categories lists the identity under the probe type and the opening cleanup deletes it.

| Check | Defect it exists for |
|---|---|
| `store_then_load`, `binary_values_round_trip`, `empty_value_is_not_missing` | a string-typed backend mangling ciphertext, an empty value reading as absent |
| `store_overwrites` | a backend that keeps the first write serves last epoch's keys forever |
| `absent_key_loads_as_none` | `KeyNotFound` where the manager expects `Ok(None)` before creating a session |
| `delete_removes_and_is_idempotent` | a second delete after a crash turning a clean recovery into a failure |
| `key_types_are_separate_namespaces`, `list_keys_is_accurate_and_scoped`, `unused_key_type_lists_empty` | categories bleeding, a group omitted from the restart listing |
| `key_ids_are_byte_exact` | a case-folding or Unicode-normalising backend keeping two peer-chosen group ids in one record |
| `key_ids_as_the_sdk_writes_them` | a `type:id` composition split back on the first colon, which loses every `session:<a>:<b>` id |
| `long_key_ids_round_trip` | a key-length limit below `GroupId::MAX_LEN` (4096), which group state is keyed by verbatim |
| `large_records_round_trip` | a value limit below a large group's ratchet tree (512 KiB probe, see below) |
| `exists_agrees_with_load` | an `exists` override that lies, so the manager mints a second identity |
| `clear_type_is_scoped_and_idempotent` | a `clear_type` that clears everything, taking the identity with the key packages |
| `concurrent_writes_land_whole` | an unlocked copy handing a reader half of one epoch and half of the next |
| `listed_records_can_all_be_deleted` | the logout contract |

The suite writes only under `mls_storage_conformance_probe*` key types and deletes everything it wrote; tests pin that a record under `identity` survives a run, including against a backend that merges key types. `clear_type` is the one check that cannot be made safe before it runs, so the docs say to probe a new backend on a scratch instance until green. Green is not a persistence test: every check runs on one open instance.

## The large-record size

Measured, not guessed: a throwaway test grew a group on a counting store. The OpenMLS `tree` record is the largest thing an `MlsStorage` sees, at about 1.1 KiB per member:

| Members | `tree` record |
|---|---|
| 65 | 74 KiB |
| 129 | 141 KiB |
| 256 (default cap) | 270 KiB |

The probe is 512 KiB. `docs/mls-integration.md` said the interface carries "key material a few hundred bytes at a time", which is what a Keychain- or preferences-backed provider would have sized itself for; corrected.

## Shape

- The report types (`ConformanceReport`, `ConformanceFailure`) move to the MLS crate and the engine re-exports them, so the two suites share one JSON shape and the FFI's existing `run_storage_conformance` is unchanged. `pass`, `fail` and `check` become public so the engine's suite can keep building its report.
- The concurrency check uses scoped threads (eight writers, sixteen overwrites each, 4 KiB values of one repeated byte per writer), so a torn read is any value that is not exactly one writer's; nothing is timed. The tearing negative control is deterministic by construction (the second distinct writer's next load must see the mix), and the negative-control test was repeated 20 times locally without a flake.

## Not in this PR

- FFI exposure. The bindings' `MlsStorageProvider` implementations are not held to the suite yet; C11 and the MLS guide say so. A `run_mls_storage_conformance(MlsStorageProvider)` mirror of the state one is a UDL change with a three-binding regeneration, so it is its own PR.
- The file-backed Rust stores (PR7 of the same program), which this suite exists to gate.

## Verification

`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --lib` (1864 in the engine, 133 in mls, all green), `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`. The measurement test was run and removed; it is not in the diff.
